headline: THE PRICE OBJECTION ON 355 COMANCHE BROKE — Monday's buyer said interested YES and priced JUST RIGHT with staging 5 of 5, the first time in this listing's life anyone has validated the number, and it happened one week after the $4,000 cut. · DO: call Ann & Don C. — the Rena agreement expires Friday · WATCH: 198 Rena listing agreement dies 8/14, two days out, still unruled at day 10.

notes: 🟢 THE FLEET CAME HOME TODAY AND CAUGHT ITSELF UP IN ONE EVENING. The Mac experiment was reversed around 3 PM and all 28 routines were re-enabled on Windows. Since 5:30 PM roughly fifteen routines have fired back-to-back — ISA briefing, four ISA sweeps, engagement, opportunity board, deep dive, inbox triage, listing folder sync, pipeline, review preview, money pulse, trading loop, CEO sweep and this console. Nothing is idle and nothing is silently dark.

🔴 ONE ROUTINE IS BLOCKED AND IT BLOCKED ITSELF ON PURPOSE. The marketing engine published nothing at 5:32 PM: it found Buffer and Gmail activity from 8/5–8/10 that this machine never wrote, concluded another machine still owned the fleet, and refused to fire catch-up posts into a double-send. That is the correct call — but it means no marketing went out today, and it stays blocked until you confirm Windows is the only machine running.

⚠️ THE REAL STORY OF THE LAST EIGHT DAYS IS SPLIT-BRAIN, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED. Every LOCAL file on this machine froze 8/4 while the fleet ran on the MacBook — ledgers, state files, showing-board dedupe records, the revenue scoreboard. Todoist and Gmail kept moving because they are cloud-side, which is exactly why nobody noticed. The CEO sweep put a number on the damage tonight: 16 scoreboard events and 427 ledger rows written on the Mac are not here. Two things followed from it in this run and both are worth knowing — the showing board's own dedupe files are eight days stale, so every alert was checked against SENT MAIL before firing rather than against the local record; and two 8/10–8/11 solid hits were found sitting completely unworked.

callBlock.who: Amber G. — she toured Comanche Monday and gave you the best form this listing has ever produced
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE NEW TOP OF THE BOARD, AND NOBODY HAS TOUCHED IT IN TWO DAYS. Her feedback landed Tuesday afternoon off the Monday 1:40 tour: interested YES · priced JUST RIGHT · staging 5 of 5 · every other field blank. ⭐ THAT IS THE FIRST 'JUST RIGHT' THIS LISTING HAS RECORDED IN ITS LIFE and the first staging 5. Every earlier read that touched the number said TOO HIGH — and all of them were filed when the list price was still $299,000. The cut to $295,000 went live 8/5. This is the first read since, and the objection is simply gone. ⭐ SHE ALSO TEXTED YOU DIRECTLY DURING THE TOUR asking whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak. An agent who asks a condition question mid-showing and then files interested YES is working a real buyer. ⚠️ HAVE THAT ANSWER READY BEFORE YOU DIAL — the question is on the record and may never have been answered. ⛔ Quote $295,000 and nothing else; she called it just right, so a discount would answer a question nobody asked. ⛔ No email went out and none was drafted — buyer's agents are the red lane under your 8/7 rule. The call is the whole product.

callBlock.who: Cassie C. and Angela B. — the two agents who called Comanche too high and STILL don't know it came down
callBlock.why: 🔴 BOTH CHIPS HAVE BEEN OVERDUE SINCE 8/8 AND AMBER G. JUST PROVED WHAT THEY ARE WORTH. Cassie's buyer toured 7/25, wrote the offer, and called $299,000 too high. Angela's buyer toured 8/2, said interested YES, and called $299,000 too high. Neither has ever been told the price moved to $295,000 — and this week a third agent looked at that same $295,000 and called it just right. ⭐ THAT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR THE CALL: you are not asking them to reconsider a number they rejected, you are telling them the number changed and a peer just validated it. ⚠️ STATED HONESTLY — Cassie's is a re-open of a dead deal at eighteen days, and that buyer may well be under contract elsewhere by now. Angela's buyer was cross-shopping a specific alternative, so the same clock applies. Both are still the cheapest at-bats on the board. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only — across six written reads not one agent has ever put a different number on paper.

callBlock.who: Wanda W. — her Saturday buyer came back 'VERY interested' on Martinwood and it has sat four days
callBlock.why: 🔥 A SOLID HIT THAT WAS ALERTED ON 8/9 AND THEN LOST IN THE HANDOVER. She filed two forms ninety seconds apart for two different showings — one buyer not interested, and one answering the interest question with the single word 'Very'. Every other field on that form was left blank, which is why the call matters: the enthusiasm is on record and the reason is not. ⭐ AND THE LISTING'S REAL OBJECTION IS NOW VERIFIED THREE WAYS, WHICH CHANGES THE STRATEGY: the stated problem is SIZE, not price. A third agent that same afternoon wrote 'Just too small.' 🔴 NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION — so the answer on this listing is audience, not number, and that is a marketing decision rather than a seller conversation. ⭐ Three showings in one Saturday on a house that had gone twenty days without one also retires the old 'this listing is invisible' read. ⛔ Call only — no email, same red-lane rule.

callBlock.who: Ann & Don C. — the Rena listing agreement expires FRIDAY and the decision is ten days unruled
callBlock.why: ⏰ TWO DAYS OUT AND THIS IS THE ONLY HARD DEADLINE ON YOUR BOARD. The choice has been sitting since 8/2: extend ninety days AND reprice to $429,900, or extend only and hold $450,000. ⭐ THE DESK'S READ IS STILL THE REPRICE — eighty-seven days at $450,000 produced exactly one offer, at $425,000, with the co-op agent volunteering that as their ceiling. ⚠️ AND THE HONEST ARGUMENT AGAINST IT LANDED THIS WEEK: a real showing ran Tuesday 8/11 at full price and you chased that agent for feedback yesterday afternoon. THAT ANSWER IS WORTH HAVING BEFORE YOU CALL — it does not change the arithmetic, because traffic without offers for eighty-seven days is what a price problem looks like, but walk in knowing both readings. ⭐ AN EXPIRED AGREEMENT IS A CLOSING YOU ALREADY PAID FOR AND THEN GAVE BACK. There are two days left to not do that.

callBlock.who: Bill R. — he opened his market report five hours ago and he is already at listing-agreement stage
callBlock.why: 🔥 THE FRESHEST SELLER SIGNAL IN THE DATABASE AND IT IS FROM TODAY. He is not a cold name — his record already sits at LISTING AGREEMENT stage, which means the relationship is well past introduction, and he chose to open your market report this afternoon. ⭐ THAT COMBINATION IS THE HIGHEST-INTENT PAIR THIS SYSTEM CAN PRODUCE: someone who has already been through the listing conversation, re-engaging with pricing content on his own initiative, unprompted. ⚠️ The lead lane was dark 8/10 through 8/12 while the fleet changed machines, so nine uncontacted leads surfaced tonight — his is the one where the relationship is furthest along and the fewest words are needed. The opener is simply the report he just read.

callBlock.who: Larry G. — he is a buyer AND a seller and you are already running his mortgage numbers by text
callBlock.why: ⭐ THE ONLY NAME ON THIS LIST THAT IS TWO DEALS AND A LOAN AT THE SAME TIME. He is hunting cheap on Lay and Logan Martin, you sent him the Highland Crest valuation, and you are working his mortgage math over text right now. ⭐ THREE LIVE THREADS WITH ONE PERSON IS NOT THREE FOLLOW-UPS, IT IS ONE CALL — and the text conversation you are already in is the warmest possible opening, because he raised the financing question himself. ⚠️ It is also the one item here where you are the lender as well as the agent, which makes the timing yours to control rather than a third party's.

callBlock.who: Damian S. — seller hand-raise Sunday, and the phone number on file is a dead end
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE SIGNAL IS REAL AND THE CHANNEL IS BROKEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS NEEDS A HUMAN. He raised his hand as a seller Sunday afternoon on a New Market property. ⛔ THE NUMBER ON HIS RECORD IS A TOLL-FREE 800 LINE — that is a lead-source artifact, not a callback number, and dialing it reaches nobody. ⭐ THE FIX IS THIRTY SECONDS: pull his real number off the CRM record first, then call. ⚠️ Nothing has gone to him on any channel yet, so the first impression is still unspent — but a Sunday seller hand-raise going cold by Thursday is the ordinary way these die.

callBlock.who: The pace number — week 34, and last week actually delivered (this is the count, not a call)
callBlock.why: 🎯 THE ONLY ITEM HERE ABOUT THE RATE RATHER THAN A DEAL. You are 22 of 45 at day 224, which annualizes to about 36. ⭐ AND THE NEWS THIS WEEK IS GENUINELY GOOD, WHICH IS RARE ON THIS LINE: week 33 delivered TWO contracts — 1709 Fieldstone at $390,000 on 8/8 and 3350 Altamont at $162,000 on 8/11, the latter from offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. That is the first time this counter has moved twice in one week all year. ⏰ THE ARITHMETIC THAT STILL GOVERNS: anything closing in 2026 has to be under contract by about October 31 at 60–75 days contract-to-close. That is eleven weeks. ⭐ AND THE INVENTORY THESIS JUST GOT EVIDENCE — two of the eight actives named nine days ago converted inside nine days. The listings you already have are the cheapest contracts available to you, which is exactly why Comanche sits at the top of this board.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $295K — THE PRICE OBJECTION BROKE, and three warm agents are unworked
listings.note: 🔥 THIS IS THE BOARD'S HEADLINE AND IT IS THE CHEAPEST CONTRACT AVAILABLE TO YOU. Monday's tour produced the first validating read in this listing's life: interested YES · priced JUST RIGHT · staging 5 of 5, the highest score it has ever recorded. ⭐ THE CAUSAL CHAIN IS CLEAN AND IT IS ON RECEIPTS: every read that ever touched the number said TOO HIGH — 7/25, 8/2, and the dead written offer — and every one of them was filed while the ask was $299,000. The $4,000 cut went live 8/5. This is the first read since, and the objection is gone. That is a $4,000 experiment that worked. ⭐ SIXTEEN SHOWINGS ALL-TIME MAKES THIS YOUR HIGHEST-TRAFFIC ACTIVE, and a seventeenth ran tonight at 5:00 — a Century 21 agent's first look, read still owed. 🔴 THE UNWORKED PART IS THE WHOLE OPPORTUNITY: three separate co-op agents have now expressed buyer interest here, and TWO OF THEM STILL DO NOT KNOW THE PRICE MOVED. Both of those chips have been overdue since 8/8. ⚠️ NOBODY HAS EVER NAMED A REPLACEMENT NUMBER — every price-recommendation field on all six reads came back blank. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only. ⚠️ One open thread from the tour: the buyer's agent asked in writing whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak, and no answer is on record.

listings.status: ⏰ Active $450K — THE LISTING AGREEMENT EXPIRES FRIDAY 8/14, two days out
listings.note: ⏰ THE ONLY HARD DEADLINE ON THE BOARD, AND THE RULING IS TEN DAYS OLD. Day 87, no price change since May, and the agreement dies Friday. The A/B has been open since 8/2: extend ninety days AND reprice to $429,900, or extend only and hold $450,000. ⭐ THE DESK'S REC IS THE REPRICE, and the evidence is the file's own history: eighty-seven days at $450,000 produced exactly one written offer, at $425,000, with the co-op agent volunteering that number as their ceiling. ⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT ARRIVED THIS WEEK AND DESERVES A HEARING: a genuine showing ran Tuesday 8/11 at 2:15 at full price, and you chased that agent for feedback yesterday afternoon. That read is worth having before the call — though traffic without offers for eighty-seven days is the textbook shape of a price problem, not a marketing one. ⚠️ ONE SHOWING WAS BOOKED AND THEN CANCELLED Sunday 8/9, which is the second time this listing has lost a confirmed appointment. ⭐ THE LEVERAGE FOR THE CONVERSATION IS UNCHANGED AND STILL GOOD: both feedback forms this house ever produced left every price field blank — the stated objections were the upstairs bathroom and a compartmentalized interior. Nobody who walked it said the number was wrong; they said the floor plan wasn't theirs. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only.

🎉 IT SOLD ITSELF, AND THE OPEN QUESTION THIS BOARD CARRIED FOR TWO WEEKS ANSWERED ITSELF WITH IT. The Mallory W. buyer — the one who said her client 'really, really liked it' but needed to save more for a down payment — DID write. Under contract 8/11 at $162,000, offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes, signed 10:19 AM. ⭐ THAT VALIDATES THE READ THIS DESK HELD AGAINST PRESSURE: the blocker was financing TIMING, not price. Every board since 8/3 said do not treat the down-payment gap as a price signal, because she wrote JUST RIGHT in the same form. She was right and the patience paid. ⏰ THE BUYER'S INSPECTION IS TOMORROW AT 10:00 AM — confirmed on the ShowingTime notice, with the MLS line already flipped to CONTINGENT. That is the next real gate on this file. ⭐ THE EXPIRING-AGREEMENT PROBLEM ON THIS UNIT IS ALSO NOW MOOT — a contract solves an expiry more permanently than an extension does. ⚠️ Contract-to-close is issued and the closing attorney and lender are named; the paragraph-30 seller initial is the live item and is tracked separately.

🎉 THE DEMAND CURVE THIS BOARD TRACKED FOR TWO WEEKS FINISHED THE JOB. One tour in its first eleven days, then six in seven days across five brokerages — and a contract at $390,000 on 8/8, which is TEN THOUSAND ABOVE the $380,000 list. ⭐ THAT NUMBER IS THE FINDING. Your own 7/17 note warned the sellers that taking $380,000 — the top of the band — 'may extend sales time.' It did not. The listing went under contract above ask inside three weeks, and the warning is now the best possible thing to have been wrong about. ⭐ THE AD THAT FED IT ALSO DID ITS JOB AND THEN CORRECTLY WENT QUIET after 8/4, so no spend is pointed at a pending listing. ⚠️ THE ONE OPERATIONAL NOTE THAT OUTLIVES THE CONTRACT: the owner-occupants cleared out three times in thirty hours during that burst without complaint. That is worth saying to them out loud before closing — it is the kind of thing sellers remember when they refer.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — THREE showings in one Saturday and a 'VERY interested' buyer unworked
listings.note: 🔥 THE LISTING THIS BOARD CALLED INVISIBLE PRODUCED THREE TOURS IN A SINGLE DAY. Saturday 8/8: three showings, three forms filed within ninety minutes of each other. One of them answered the interest question with the single word 'Very' — every other field blank. ✅ AND TWO LONG-STANDING BOARD ITEMS CLOSE HERE. First, the $5,000 cut the seller approved back in July is now VERIFIED LIVE AND PUBLIC — the MLS line on all three notices reads $184,000, so the old 'unverified, do not quote' hedge is retired and the number is quotable. Second, the twenty-days-without-a-showing silence is over. 🔴 THE REAL FINDING IS THE OBJECTION, AND IT IS VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the problem is SIZE, not price. The clearest of the three reads says it in four words — 'Just too small.' ⛔ NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION. That means the answer on this listing is AUDIENCE, not number — point it at first-time buyers, downsizers and investors — and it means a price conversation with this seller would be solving the wrong problem. This board argued for a cut here for weeks on the strength of silence; the showings arrived and said something different, and the earlier read is withdrawn. 🔴 The ad on this listing has produced zero leads in ten days after being the best performer on record in July.

listings.status: 🔴 Under contract $899K — no fresh receipt in eight days, treat the close date as unverified
listings.note: ⚠️ THE BIGGEST DEAL ON THE BOARD IS ALSO THE ONE THIS RUN CAN SAY LEAST ABOUT, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING. Nothing has crossed this desk on this file since 8/4 — no ShowingTime notice, no milestone, no correspondence in the fourteen-day window. ⛔ THE LAST RECEIPTED CLOSE DATE WAS 8/14, WHICH IS THE DAY AFTER TOMORROW, and the buyer's side had asked to push it to Aug 20 with no signed amendment ever appearing on any lane here. THAT ASK WAS NEVER RESOLVED IN ANYTHING THIS DESK CAN READ. ⚠️ Eight days of split-brain sits directly across that gap, so absence of a receipt here means the machine was looking at the wrong disk, NOT that the file went quiet. Do not read this row as 'nothing happened' — read it as 'this desk cannot see.' ⭐ WHAT REMAINS VERIFIED AND GOOD: the appraisal is complete and clean on the lender's own words, which removes your financing risk from the date question entirely; the repair addendum is fully executed; and the septic inspection ran 8/4. ⛔ Do not print Aug 20 as the close date on any surface — 8/14 is the last receipted one and an unagreed six-day push is an ask, not an agreement. 🔴 THIS FILE NEEDS A COORDINATOR CHECK TOMORROW MORNING, ahead of everything else on this row.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract — inspection AND appraisal both cleared, close receipted 8/31
listings.note: ✅ THE CLEANEST FILE ON YOUR BOARD AND IT GOT CLEANER DURING THE DARK WINDOW. Two gates cleared while nobody was watching: the inspection ran Wednesday 8/5 at noon and the appraisal ran Friday 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both confirmed on primary notices, with the MLS line reading CONTINGENT throughout. ⭐ AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH BEHIND YOU BY DAY TWENTY IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL ON THIS BOARD OCCUPIES — the two events that kill contracts are spent, and the close is receipted 8/31. ⚠️ ONE ADMINISTRATIVE THREAD WAS LEFT UNSIGNED ON 8/4 — an address-correction addendum shared on dotloop that sat twenty-nine hours without a signature receipt. It has not been re-checked since and should be confirmed closed before the file is called clean. ⚠️ ONE NUMBER REMAINS UNRULED and it is worth real money on an otherwise settled deal: the buyer's agent asked for a 3.5% co-op commission and nobody has ever answered. That is a decision, not a chore. ⭐ The client side is fully handled — both sellers completed, and the congratulations-and-what-happens-next letter went out walking the earnest money and the inspection, financing and appraisal clocks.

listings.status: ✅ Active $559K — still drawing tours, and the price reads are now split
listings.note: ✅ IT KEPT PRODUCING TRAFFIC THROUGH THE WHOLE DARK WINDOW — a tour on 8/4 and another Monday 8/10 at 2:00, on a listing that has taken forty showings all-time and was relisted after the prior contract was mutually released. ⚠️ THE 8/4 READ IS THE FIRST ONE THAT HURTS AND IT DESERVES TO BE STATED PLAINLY: interested No · priced TOO HIGH · staging 2 out of 5. ⭐ THAT STAGING SCORE IS THE ACTIONABLE HALF, NOT THE PRICE HALF. A 2 is the lowest this listing has ever recorded, against a 4 three weeks earlier from an agent who called the price JUST RIGHT — the house did not get more expensive between those two visits, it got less presentable. 🔴 AND IT CORROBORATES THE ITEM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED UNACTIONED FOR THREE WEEKS: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL. An electrician and a cleaner are still cheaper than another lost buyer, and 'glitching' on a house whose contract was released for a reason nobody here has ever established may be the answer to what killed it. ⚠️ THE PRICE EVIDENCE IS NOW GENUINELY SPLIT — two reads said just right, two said too high, and not one of the four has ever named a replacement number. ⛔ Do not take a price conversation to this institutional seller off a split record. ⚠️ Quote $559,000 only.

listings.status: 🆕 Coming to market — photographer wanted MONDAY, agreement is OUT but NOT SIGNED
listings.note: 🆕 THE TWO-SIDED DEAL THIS BOARD CHASED FOR A WEEK IN JULY IS NOW A REAL LISTING, AND IT HAS A SEQUENCING PROBLEM. Sondra wrote at 3:29 yesterday afternoon: 'We do want the photographer to come Monday, if possible.' ⚠️ AND THE CROSS-CHECK IS THE WHOLE POINT — the listing agreement went out for signature but is NOT SIGNED YET. Booking a photographer against an unsigned agreement is how the shoot slips, and this exact sequence already cost time on the Deer Ridge file two days earlier. ⭐ THE MOVE IS TO CLOSE THE SIGNATURE FIRST AND BOOK THE SHOOT IN THE SAME CONVERSATION, not to answer the photographer question in isolation. ⚠️ THE PRICE IS STILL UNVERIFIED ANYWHERE ON THIS DESK — no number has ever appeared on a receipt, so nothing may quote one. ⭐ Worth remembering what this relationship actually is: she came in unprompted off a listing alert saying they were very interested in a property AND about ready to list their own. This is the LIST half of a two-sided deal, and the buy half has never been worked.

listings.status: 🆕 Active $599K package — the only ad in the portfolio producing anything
listings.note: 🆕 THE NEWEST INVENTORY ON THE BOARD AND THE ONLY MARKETING SPEND THAT IS CURRENTLY WORKING. The nineteen-lot package went live 8/11 and has produced four buyer signals in three days — while every other ad in the portfolio produced zero. ⭐ ONE OF THOSE NAMES IS WORTH A SECOND LOOK BEFORE HE IS TREATED AS A RETAIL BUYER: one respondent works at an auction company, which is a different conversation entirely on a nineteen-lot package — that is a bulk-disposition call, not a lot sale. 🔴 THE OPEN ITEM IS A BUILDER QUESTION THAT HAS SAT ABOUT ELEVEN HOURS: a land company principal asked in writing yesterday morning whether the lots have had septic perc testing, and no answer has gone back. A holding answer with the blocks-and-takedown option is drafted but unsent. ⚠️ THAT QUESTION IS THE GATE ON THE WHOLE PACKAGE — perc results decide buildability, which decides price per lot, and a builder who does not get an answer assumes the worst. ⭐ Blocks and takedowns at a higher per-lot number remain acceptable per the seller's own ruling; the single-package listing at $599,000 is the anchor, not the only shape.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — biggest listing in the book, and the seller identity is STILL unverified
listings.note: ⚠️ THE LARGEST NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD IS ALSO THE ONE WITH THE WEAKEST FILE, AND THAT COMBINATION HAS NOW SURVIVED TWO WEEKS. No showing, no feedback and no correspondence has crossed this desk on this address in the entire fourteen-day window. ⛔ THE CLIENT IDENTITY REMAINS UNVERIFIED under the identity law — a name is carried in memory, and memory is not a receipt. On a $1.15M listing that is not a formality: it gates every piece of client-facing creative and every seller email. ⭐ THE POSITIONING READ IS STILL THE MOST USEFUL THING ON THE FILE and it has not been improved on: the only tour this listing ever took said, verbatim, 'He likes the house but the land isn't what he is looking for.' The objection is ACREAGE, which on a listing at this price is the cheapest possible loss — nobody has said it is too expensive. ⭐ THE UNANSWERED QUESTION IS THEREFORE A TARGETING ONE: who is the buyer that wants THIS land, and is the marketing pointed at them. ⏰ The open house held 8/2 was never debriefed and its sign-in sheet has never been captured — nine days on, that is effectively lost. 🛑 The security item on this address stands unchanged: the lookalike meeting link is not to be opened, on any device.

listings.status: 🔴 Buyer-side $2.35M — the counter has never been put on paper, and it is 22 days now
listings.note: 🔴 THE LARGEST SINGLE NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD, ROUGHLY $36K OF GCI, AND THE WHOLE COST OF MOVING IT IS TWENTY MINUTES OF WRITING. The listing side has asked repeatedly since 7/21 to be moved forward and has never received a written position from your side. ⚠️ STATED HONESTLY: a phone call leaves no receipt, so this is ABSENCE rather than proven failure — but what was promised was paper, and there is none on any lane this desk can read. ⭐ WHY IT KEEPS RETURNING: a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal, and the honest answer IS the counter. Sending it is not a favour to them; it is your position on the record. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED, AND THIS MATTERS BEFORE ANYTHING GOES OVER: the appraisal figure your buyer cited as roughly 40% under ask is single-sourced from him. Whose appraisal it is, when it was done, and whether it is a formal appraisal at all are all unknown. Do not quote it to the other side as an appraised value. ⚠️ Three feedback requests from the listing side also remain unanswered.

✅ THE TABLE RAN 8/4 AT 2:00 PM AND THE FILE IS DONE. Six days of 'which day is it actually' ended on schedule. ⚠️ ONE ADMINISTRATIVE LOOSE END NEVER RESOLVED AND IS NOW PERMANENT HISTORY RATHER THAN A LIVE ITEM: the extension addendum the listing side promised on 7/28 never appeared on any receipt this desk holds. The date held anyway. ⚠️ AND ONE COURTESY WAS NEVER PAID: three feedback requests from the other side's listing agent went unanswered before the close. That is now a shrug at an agent you just closed a deal with rather than a task — worth thirty seconds of repair if her path crosses yours again, because that is exactly the agent who sends the next co-op deal. ✅ The MLS line flipping CONTINGENT to EXPIRED was correctly recorded as a question and not an alarm — you were buyer-side, so that was the seller's listing term lapsing alongside a live contract.
